question: Which coordinate-basis properties explain Adam's advantage on transformers, given that its elementwise adaptivity is not rotation invariant?

key_findings.claim: Function-preserving parameter rotations can severely degrade Adam while leaving SGD invariant up to numerical effects.
key_findings.evidence: The study inserts orthogonal reparameterizations and maps updates back to the original function. Broader rotations hurt more: reported global rotations slow GPT-2 training by 16% and ViT by 96%, while output-wise rotations preserve more canonical structure and perform near the unrotated basis.

key_findings.claim: SVD-derived layer rotations can preserve or improve Adam performance, showing that the canonical basis is useful but not uniquely optimal.
key_findings.evidence: Rotations built from recent gradient or moment singular vectors are recomputed periodically and outperform random global rotations; some improve on no rotation. The procedure is intentionally diagnostic and has substantial SVD overhead, not a proposed production optimizer.

key_findings.claim: Several published coordinate-dependent assumptions fail to rank the tested rotations in the same order as Adam performance.
key_findings.evidence: The paper measures coordinate smoothness, gradient concentration, and noise-related quantities. None consistently explains unrotated, output-wise, input-wise, layer-wise, global, and SVD cases, supporting the criticism that rotation-invariant analyses cannot distinguish them at all.

key_findings.claim: Near-semi-orthogonality of matrix updates correlates with performance across rotations but is not shown to cause it.
key_findings.evidence: The coefficient of variation of nonzero singular values is lowest for SVD rotations and highest for full rotations, aligning with loss. Recomputing the SVD every 250 steps produces abrupt changes in the statistic. The authors explicitly leave a rigorous account of why orthogonality helps and why Adam induces it open.

method.core_idea: Use function-preserving rotations as controlled interventions that expose what elementwise Adam exploits about the standard parameter basis.
method.mechanism: Rotate matrix parameter coordinates at different scopes, transform gradients and updates consistently, compare Adam and SGD on GPT-2, ViT, and ResNet, construct SVD-aligned rotations, and measure candidate rotation-dependent statistics including update singular-value dispersion.
assumptions: The rotated implementations are functionally and numerically comparable.
Hyperparameters tuned in one basis remain a fair diagnostic in another.
Singular-value coefficient of variation is a meaningful measure of scaled orthogonality.
The tested architectures span relevant Adam-versus-SGD regimes.
Performance changes are not dominated by kernel or FlashAttention implementation differences.

techniques.role: Changes Adam's coordinate system without changing the represented network.
Separates output-, input-, layer-, and global-coordinate structure.
Searches for bases better aligned to recent optimization geometry.
Ranks matrix updates by singular-value dispersion.

evaluations.baseline: Adam in the canonical parameter basis

evaluations.metric: Sensitivity of Adam and relative SGD behavior
evaluations.result: Much smaller rotation sensitivity than transformers

evaluations.metric: Loss versus singular-value coefficient of variation
evaluations.result: More semi-orthogonal updates correlate with better performance

limitations: Author-stated: SVD rotation is diagnostic, not a practical optimizer.
Author-stated: update orthogonality has no causal or convergence guarantee.
Author-stated: why SVD rotations improve orthogonality remains unexplained.
Reviewer-identified: fixed hyperparameters may disadvantage rotations with different effective scaling.
Reviewer-identified: slowdown percentages depend on chosen horizon, loss target, and implementation.
failure_modes: Rotation kernels change numerical precision or systems efficiency rather than optimization alone.
Retuning epsilon and learning rate erases the reported basis ranking.
Update orthogonality is an epiphenomenon of lower loss.
An SVD basis overfits recent gradients and destabilizes later phases.
Vector and embedding parameters do not follow matrix-layer conclusions.
Architectural parameterizations change the canonical-basis advantage.
reusable_insights: Test adaptive-optimizer theories on function-preserving coordinate changes they claim should not matter.
Distinguish rotation-invariant convergence guarantees from explanations of practical advantage.
Use a scope ladder to localize which coordinate structure is beneficial.
Intervene directly on update singular values before treating orthogonality as causal.
Retune basis-sensitive numerical hyperparameters in a secondary fairness audit.
open_questions: Can controlled orthogonalization improve Adam without periodic SVD?
Why are transformer canonical coordinates more useful than ResNet coordinates?
Does update semi-orthogonality predict performance prospectively across optimizers?
How do epsilon, weight decay, normalization, and tensor shape affect rotation sensitivity?
Can theory express coordinate structure without vacuous worst-case constants?

competitive_landscape.title: The Marginal Value of Adaptive Gradient Methods in Machine Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Wilson et al. show adaptive methods can generalize differently from SGD and emphasize parameterization effects. This paper isolates basis dependence with explicit function-preserving rotations on transformers and seeks a geometric explanatory statistic.

competitive_landscape.title: Noise Is Not the Main Factor Behind the Gap Between SGD and Adam on Transformers, but Sign Descent Might Be
competitive_landscape.difference: Kunstner et al. attribute much of the transformer gap to sign-like updates rather than noise. The rotation study asks which basis makes coordinatewise sign/adaptive behavior effective and points toward matrix-update orthogonality.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
competitive_landscape.difference: Reddi et al. expose failure modes and derive AMSGrad-style guarantees under coordinate assumptions. The present work argues that such guarantees do not explain why the canonical transformer basis is empirically favorable.

competitive_landscape.title: AdaMuon: Adaptive Muon Optimizer
competitive_landscape.difference: AdaMuon explicitly combines elementwise adaptation and orthogonalized updates and reports large-scale efficiency gains. It operationalizes the geometry this paper identifies correlationally, making it important later competition to the proposed research direction.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Adam's practical transformer advantage requires rotation-dependent explanation, and scaled update orthogonality is a promising missing quantity.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Controlled rotations reveal large basis effects, structured/SVD bases can help, prior statistics fail, and update singular-value dispersion tracks performance across interventions.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Basis sensitivity of coordinatewise adaptive methods is known, but the scope-controlled transformer experiments and orthogonality correlation are valuable. The paper diagnoses a gap rather than closing it: orthogonality is neither theoretically justified nor causally validated.

reviewer_notes: Read all 42 extracted pages, including review appendix, rotation construction, main GPT/ViT/ResNet results, assumption audits, orthogonality plots, algorithm variants, and Muon discussion. Four primary arXiv records, including later AdaMuon, were checked on 2026-08-23.
